newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl will speak to Yeltsin later this week.
newsitem.headline: Kohl will speak to Yeltsin later this week.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Thursday he had not spoken to Russian President Boris Yeltsin since their meeting last Saturday but he planned to speak to him on Friday or during the weekend.

Kohl told reporters in Bonn the Russian leader, who was admitted to hospital on Wednesday suffering from the first signs of pneumonia, had clearly been suffering from a cold during their meeting but had been mentally alert.

"I haven't spoken to Boris Yeltsin but I had agreed with him that we would speak on the phone on Friday of this week or the weekend that followed," Kohl told reporters. "He already had the cold. That was clearly visible."
Kohl said the Russian president had shown he was still mentally agile, referring to previous conversations the two leaders had held and using few briefing aids.
"He was totally mentally alert," the chancellor said. "He discussed the issues with me for two hours.
Kohl added Yeltsin's chances of a return to normal health were good as long as he took things easy. "One thing is very important. He wants to carry out the duties of his office," he said.
